chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'Does the man recite the Adhan while he is not facing the Qiblah?' He said, 'If the Tashahhud is facing the Qiblah, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to face the Qiblah while reciting the Adhan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in the direction of the Mu'adhin, ruling that facing the Qiblah specifically during the Tashahhud segment is sufficient for validity. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the ritual act of calling to prayer and the strict orientation required for the prayer itself, emphasizing ease (*rukhsah*) in the Adhan's performance. The hadith underscores the importance of the declaration of faith within the call, linking the physical orientation to the spiritual intent of the testimony.
